periods.analysis: The Community Wellness & Prevention Program is green at 15% complete, establishing a solid prevention base for Harborview’s fast-growing population. Mobile clinic routes launched as planned, with Route A covering Bayside Terrace and Harborview Station on Tuesdays and Route B reaching Northpoint, Pelican Cove, and the marina workforce lots on Thursdays. The school vaccination drive is in progress, and the chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, which is appropriate at this early stage while we stabilize outreach flow and referral protocols.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the two mobile clinic routes for the next quarter and add a simple weekly dashboard for visits, vaccines offered, vaccines accepted, and referrals by census tract. Keep the school vaccination drive moving by locking nurse staffing with Harborview Unified for the first four campus events. Prepare, but do not yet launch, chronic-disease screening by finalizing consent forms, lab vendor pricing, and referral pathways to community primary-care partners.

periods.analysis: The program remains green and moved up 5 percentage points, from 15% to 20% complete. Mobile clinic routes continue to perform as the dependable front door, especially for families in Bayside Terrace and older adults near Pelican Cove, where the public health nurses are seeing repeat engagement rather than one-time contact. The school vaccination drive is still in progress, and the chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, so the work is advancing in the right sequence: access first, prevention uptake second, expanded screening third.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the current mobile clinic cadence and extend one evening stop per month at Harborview Station to reach service workers after shift change. For the school vaccination drive, prioritize completion of the remaining consent packets through bilingual robocalls and backpack notices before winter break. Begin a readiness checklist for chronic-disease screening that identifies the first three pilot sites and the minimum data set for blood pressure, A1c risk, and tobacco-use counseling.

periods.analysis: The initiative is green at 25% complete, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter increase from 20%. Winter respiratory season increased demand on the mobile units, but the team kept prevention visible by pairing vaccine counseling with basic health navigation at the Shoreline Library and Northpoint Community Room stops. The school vaccination drive remains in progress, and the chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, which keeps the program focused on completing the current prevention cohort before adding new clinical workflows.
periods.recommendations: Sustain mobile route reliability by assigning a backup medical assistant pool for weather or sick-call disruptions, especially on coastal route days. Use the school drive’s current momentum to schedule make-up clinics at the three campuses with the highest unsigned consent rates. Advance chronic-disease screening preparation by selecting a lab interface vendor and drafting standing orders for nurse-led blood pressure and diabetes-risk checks.

periods.analysis: Performance remains green at 30% complete, up 5 points from 25% in the prior quarter. Spring outreach benefited from park and recreation partnerships, with the mobile clinic colocating at Saturday youth sports registration at Mariner Fields and at the Seabreeze Senior Walk program. The school vaccination drive is still in progress, and chronic-disease screening expansion is still not started, but the operational foundation is stronger because the team now has a clearer map of under-immunized school cohorts and high-need neighborhoods.
periods.recommendations: Continue the mobile clinic schedule and add two prevention-focused pop-up days tied to summer meal distribution sites. For the school vaccination drive, segment outreach by grade band and campus so nurses can focus on the students closest to compliance deadlines. Complete the chronic-disease screening implementation plan this quarter, including pilot-site staffing, point-of-care equipment inventory, and warm handoff agreements with two federally qualified health center partners.

periods.analysis: The program is green at 35% complete, another 5-point increase from 30%, and the year-over-year arc is steady rather than episodic. Back-to-school season is giving the school vaccination drive a practical lift, with Harborview Unified nurses and city public health staff coordinating campus lists before the first exclusion notices are needed. Mobile clinic routes remain complete and active, while chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, so we should treat this quarter as the bridge between vaccination operations and the next prevention layer.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the mobile routes and add a back-to-school vaccine counseling script at every stop through September. Concentrate school vaccination work on the remaining in-progress campus cohorts, using Saturday clinics at East Harbor High and Vista Point Middle to reduce transportation barriers. Prepare chronic-disease screening launch materials now, including resident-facing plain-language handouts and a referral tracker that flags uninsured residents for benefits navigation.

periods.analysis: The initiative remains green at 40% complete, up 5 points from 35% last quarter. The mobile clinics are now a familiar part of Harborview’s prevention infrastructure, and staff report that residents are arriving with family members and medication lists, which is a sign of trust and repeat use. The school vaccination drive is still in progress and chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, but the program is maturing in a controlled way without overextending clinical capacity during the holiday and respiratory-virus period.
periods.recommendations: Keep the mobile clinic routes intact through winter and add flu and COVID booster reminders to appointment cards and text-message follow-ups. For the school vaccination drive, schedule targeted catch-up clinics before winter break and assign one data analyst to reconcile school rosters against city clinic records. Finalize chronic-disease screening procurement for cuffs, scales, and A1c testing supplies so the expansion can begin from a ready position when authorized.

periods.analysis: The program is green at 45% complete, a 5-point gain from 40% in 2025-Q4. This quarter shows the benefit of disciplined prevention work: mobile clinic routes are complete and functioning, school vaccination remains in progress with better roster reconciliation, and residents increasingly know where to find services before a health issue becomes urgent. Chronic-disease screening expansion is still not started, which is the main sequencing item to watch, but it is not a performance concern as long as readiness tasks continue to close.
periods.recommendations: Sustain current mobile service levels and test a reminder-and-return protocol for residents who receive vaccine counseling but defer the shot. Push the school vaccination drive by producing weekly campus exception lists for principals, nurses, and the public health liaison. Move chronic-disease screening from planning to launch readiness by training the first nurse cohort on blood pressure technique, diabetes-risk screening, documentation, and referral escalation.

periods.analysis: The Community Wellness & Prevention Program remains green at 50% complete, up 5 points from 45% last quarter and 35 points from the 15% starting point in 2024-Q3. Mobile clinic routes are complete and have become the stable delivery platform for prevention in Harborview’s coastal neighborhoods, while the school vaccination drive continues in progress with a clearer operating rhythm. Chronic-disease screening expansion remains not started, so the next half of the initiative should convert the access model we have built into broader prevention services without losing the reliability residents now expect.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the mobile clinic network and extend one route to a rotating summer schedule at the ferry terminal, youth recreation sites, and senior housing courtyards. Set a closeout plan for the school vaccination drive with campus-specific targets, final consent outreach, and documented handoffs for students who need primary-care follow-up. Authorize the chronic-disease screening pilot at three prepared sites, beginning with blood pressure and diabetes-risk checks, and review uptake, referral completion, and equity by neighborhood after the first 60 days.

periods.analysis: 95% complete. 2 of 3 milestones are done. Next up: Chronic-disease screening expansion (due Oct 24, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
